author: TEDx Talks
description:
We often allow other people’s words, failures, and past experiences to define who we believe we are. Through the powerful story of an eagle raised among chickens, this talk explores how limiting beliefs can hide our true potential. Drawing from his own experiences with speech difficulties, insecurity, rejection, and failure, the speaker reveals how changing his self-image and inner dialogue transformed his life.

At the heart of the talk is the STAR framework—seeing yourself differently and talking to yourself differently—along with the reminder that an event is not an identity and a setback is not an ending. The talk invites us to question the stories we have accepted about ourselves and recognize the potential that has always been within us. Because sometimes, we don't need new wings—we simply need to see ourselves differently. Cyril Joseph is a professional who bridges the gap between professional excellence and personal purpose. With over 17 years of cross-industry experience span
title: Change your perspective, change your possibilities | Cyril Joseph | TEDxMoulsari Avenue

description: Many of us are taught that if we work hard and follow the right path, we will build a successful life. But today that path feels far less certain. Author and future-of-learning expert Janine Mathó reveals the hidden gap between how we prepare people for success and what today's world demands of us. This talk presents a hopeful new way to think about success, uncertainty, and what it takes to create a life that is truly our own. Janine Mathó is an internationally recognized learning and leadership expert with more than twenty-five years of experience spanning education, leadership development, organizational transformation, and the future of work. A former executive at Harvard University and Pearson, she has dedicated her career to helping individuals and organizations navigate complex change and build capabilities required for the future. She currently serves as Chief Learning Officer at Dreamtime Learning Asia and is an author, advisor, and keynote speaker. Her work combines learning
title: How to create a life that’s really yours | Janine Matho | TEDxEuro School Whitefield

Brett Brewer helped build the platform that took social media mainstream. Now he's here to say what the industry won't: that the crisis in youth mental health is not an accident, that the companies claiming nothing can be done aren't telling the truth, and that the people with the most power to fix this have billions of reasons not to. In this talk, he breaks the silence that most founders keep: about what they saw happening to users as early as 2003, what they chose to call success, and what we owe the generation of children who grew up inside what they built. He also comes with something most critics don't have
title: What social media platforms don’t want you to know | Brett Brewer | TEDxUCLA

As CEO of Prepr, he builds programs equipping youth and organizations with skills in AI, innovation, and entrepreneurship, advising governments companies while advancing inclusive, future-ready innovation ecosystems.  Angeline Virginia Wong is an 18-year-old director, designer, singer-songwriter, actress, model, and youth leader. Multidisipliner sanatçı, performans yönetmeni ve tasarımcı Birim Erol, sanata çocuk yaşlarda annesi Ressam Semra Baykal’ın yönlendirmesiyle adım attı. description: This talk examines how Aretha Franklin navigated the tension between a rebellious artistic identity and the pressures of social integration. By exploring her role in soul music, Black cultural movements, and the challenges faced by Black artists within a structurally unequal society, the talk reveals how artistic expression can become a strategic tool for both resistance and inclusion. Hello, I am Binru Yang, currently a grade 11 student. I characterize myself as a dedicated learner—fascinated by the depth of knowledge within each subject, the value of connecting theoretical learning to real-world scenarios, and the pursuit of opportunities that expand my academic horizons and critical thinking skills. description:
As AI continues to blur the line between creation and replication, Jiale Weng responds with three works—Activation, Paradise Lost, and his Scroll Installation Series—asking: What still belongs to us as human beings?
His answer comes down to three words: encounter, choice, and gaze. The presence of the body, the choices we make with hesitation and responsibility, and the imagination we leave for memory—these are what make us human, and what cannot be replaced.
当AI不断模糊创作与复制的边界，翁嘉乐用《激活》《失乐园》和长卷装置系列三件作品回应：什么仍然属于人？他把答案凝成三个词——相遇、选择、凝视。身体的在场、犹豫与责任的选择、留给记忆的想象，才是人之所以为人、无法被替代的部分。
 A artist focused on installation and public art with a cross-disciplinary approach. Works have been featured in exhibitions including the 3rd China International Kinetic Sculpture Exhibition, Through the Body: Robotics Art in China, Fission: The Global Wave of Digital Art, and the Invitational Exhibition of Chinese Contemporary Kinetic Sculpture. Recipient of the Tomorrow Sculpture Award and Yang Xiaoyang Award, with
title: The stronger our technology, the more invaluable our humanity | Jiale Weng | TEDxNew Channel Qingdao

author: TEDx Talks
description: We're taught early to sort people into columns: hero or villain, good or bad, rarely both. This talk pulls that instinct apart through the lens of great literature: from Frankenstein’s Creature to Achilles, it shows how the characters we remember the most are never just one thing. They’re often both aspects in the same breath. It then turns that same lens on real life- asking why we extend fictional characters the patience to be complicated but deny real people the same. Rooted in this year’s theme, Beyond the Binary, the talk argues that the binary itself is fiction; the more honest and realistic story is the one where good and bad simply refuse to separate. Aripra is an IBDP student at Chirec, studying Maths AA, Economics and Physics as her Higher Levels. Off stage, she’s usually rewatching Brooklyn 99 for the fifth time or blasting Green Day like it's her life motto. Ask her what she identifies with most and there’s a high chance she’ll throw a John Green quote your way: "I go to s
title: There Are No Villains In Great Literature | Aripra Sharma | TEDxOakridge Gachibowli

author: TEDx Talks
description: Naithik's TEDx talk focuses on the Halo effect, which is a cognitive bias where a perception of one trait influences how we judge an overall brand, individual or product. This topic seamlessly aligns with this year’s theme of "Beyond the Binary” as it explains to the audience how we categorize things as traditional opposites. By understanding the Halo Effect, individuals can become more aware of their own unconscious biases, consider multiple perspectives before forming opinions, and make fairer and more thoughtful conclusions. This talk offers a new opinion on how greater awareness of our own thinking can lead to balanced decisions, relationships and a richer understanding of the people and ideas that shape our lives. Naithik Reddy is an IB MYP - 5 student who is passionate about making progressive changes to the world. He is an enthusiast in economics and astronomy, and one day wants to help build a spaceship that is capable of travelling at the speed of light. A confident public sp
title: The Truth Behind False Judgements | Sree Naithik Reddy Rakasi | TEDxOakridge Gachibowli

author: TEDx Talks
description: Wonder why we instinctively ask people to choose? Science or religion. Logic or emotion. Fact or faith. We often assume that opposing perspectives cannot coexist, but what if they were never meant to compete? In this talk, Saisha Kodali reflects on how growing up with Hindu mythology, studying physics, and living in a community of over 80 nationalities challenged her understanding of truth. Through stories of childhood wonder, friendships that transformed headlines into human experiences, and the surprising lessons hidden in something as ordinary as fire, she explores how different perspectives can illuminate the same reality. Beyond the Binary is an invitation to replace certainty with curiosity, to embrace complexity over simplicity, and to discover that our richest understanding of the world often emerges not by choosing one perspective over another, but by allowing them to exist together. Saisha Kodali is an IBDP Year 2 student at UWC ISAK Japan taking Higher Level Physics, Mathem
title: Facts and Stories: Rethinking the Way We Know | Saisha Kodali | TEDxOakridge Gachibowli

The talk explores how ideas find us, create a domino effect, and influence the way we interpret our experiences. It highlights the shift from a fixed mindset, where failure is seen as proof of inability, to a growth mindset, where failure becomes evidence of where we can grow.

The talk encourages us to share our ideas, act before we feel ready, and sit with discomfort. It ultimately invites us to ask the powerful question, “What if?”—and consider how one idea, when pursued with courage and an open mind, can change everything. 17-year-old Student Leader

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the greatest illusion isn’t created by a magician – but by our own minds?

Every day, we divide the world into neat categories. These mental shortcuts help us make sense of reality, but they also blind us to its complexity. Through the art of magic, psychology, and interactive demonstrations, Dr. Ramya Sri Gunturu invites the audience to experience how easily perception can be manipulated and how confidently we can believe things that are not true.

In a talk that is both thought provoking and entertaining, she explores why our minds crave certainty, how these invisible cognitive illusions shape our judgements, relationships and identities, and why moving beyond binary thinking is essential for empathy, growth and meaningful human connection. By the end, the audience won’t just question what they see – they’ll question the assumptions they’ve been living by. Dr. Ramya Sri Gunturu is an international magician, psychologist, educator, life skills trainer and world record holder
title: The Greatest Illusion: The Mind | Dr. Ramya Sri Gunturu | TEDxOakridge Gachibowli

description:
In a world where first impressions often shape the way we see others, how often do we allow one observation to become a conclusion?

Reyaan’s talk explores the invisible boundaries created when people are placed into simple categories based on what is immediately visible. Through personal experiences and reflections, he will examine how assumptions can influence the way we perceive ability, identity, and potential. The talk will explore the importance of looking “Beyond the Binary” by understanding the importance of looking beyond fixed labels and recognising the complexity of every person. 

This talk will make the audience question the boundaries they create, challenge the stories they write too quickly, and consider what they might find when they look beyond the first impression. Reyaan Aditya Villa is an IBDP-1 student at Oakridge, with a strong interest in finance, business, technology, and creating meaningful social impact. He also enjoys cricket, leadership, theatre, and Model
title: The Story We Write Too Soon | Reyaan Aditya Villa | TEDxOakridge Gachibowli

What followed was not a magic act. It was a precise, personal argument about the rules most people live by without ever choosing them. Drawing on his journey as a silent immigrant child who found connection through magic, and a decade of performing for Google, Netflix, Amazon, and Bvlgari, Wu asks the question most success stories are afraid to ask: who actually wrote the rule you are living by? Johnny Wu is a celebrity mentalist and keynote speaker known for blending illusion with powerful insights on identity, ambition, and performance. With over 2,000 five-star reviews and performances for brands like Google, Netflix, Amazon, and Bvlgari, Johnny brings both credibility and depth to the stage.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A primeira palestra realizada com os olhos em um TEDx.
Aos 25 anos, um AVC isquêmico deixou Elaine Luzia tetraplégica e sem fala. Consciente de tudo, sem conseguir expressar nada. Estudante de medicina no terceiro ano, ela passou a ser tratada como incapaz, embora nada tivesse mudado na sua capacidade de raciocinar.
A virada começou na UTI, com uma prancha alfabética: letra por letra, piscando os olhos. Nove anos depois, ela reuniu de novo a própria voz. Voltou à universidade, concluiu medicina, passou em concurso e hoje atua como perita médica federal.
Aqui ela defende uma tese incômoda: a sociedade ainda mede competência pelo som da voz, e por isso desperdiça inteligência que só espera um meio de se expressar.
Elaine Luzia é médica, farmacêutica, perita médica federal.
No espírito das "ideias que merecem ser espalhadas" o TED criou o TEDx. TEDx é um programa de eventos organizados localmente, que reúnem pessoas para compartilhar uma experiência ao estilo TED. Nosso evento é chamado
title: Quantas inteligências estão em silêncio? | Elaine Luzia dos Santos | TEDxFortaleza

description: When we think of violence, we remember the incident. But for survivors, the second assault often comes from our headlines, our questions, and our silence. Indu Gopalakrishnan is the founder of Project Kintsugi, a transformative support community dedicated to providing safe spaces, guidance, and resilience-building tools for women navigating marital challenges, including divorce and domestic violence. Born from her own lived experience, Indu turned personal hardship into purpose, creating a platform that encourages healing, connection, and empowerment for women facing societal stigma and emotional overwhelm. What began as a personal journey has grown into a community where women share strength, find confidence, and rediscover direction together.  Alexandre Delgado estudou composição com Joly Braga Santos e foi aluno de Jacques Charpentier em França, onde se diplomou com o 1.º Prémio de Composição do Conservatório de Nice.

A sua carreira foi projectada pelo êxito internacional da ópera O Doido e a Morte (1994), que dirigiu em Lisboa, Berlim, Belém do Pará e Rio de Janeiro.

description:
"Ben aklın duyarlılığında mı, yoksa toplumsal gerçekliğin duyarlılığında mı yaşıyorum?" Dr. Zeliha Bürtek, konuşmasının başlığını "Rota: Bir Keçi Yolu mudur?" koydu. Ona göre keçi yolu, herkesin kendi başına yürüdüğü bir patikaydı ve bu patika aslında yazgının, kaderin ta kendisiydi.

Konuşmasında iki farklı duyarlılığı karşı karşıya koydu: Aklın duyarlılığı, ahlakın yön verdiği, mahremin korunduğu bir yerdi. Toplumsal gerçekliğin duyarlılığıysa, mahremin ve yalnızlığın saklanamadığı, çırılçıplak bir aidiyetsizlikti. Ona göre bugün hepimiz bu iki gerilim arasında sıkışmış durumdaydık.

Bir kadın olarak, metropolde doğup büyüdüğünü, yalnız yaşadığını ve tüm kararlarını kimseye sormadan aldığını anlattı. Karanlık sokaklarda saatlerce sokak hayvanlarını besleyen "korkusuz kadın" kimliğiyle, vicdanının her zaman yol arkadaşı olduğunu söyledi. Ama bugün asıl sorduğu soru şuydu: O vicdana kim, hangi cüretle müdahale ediyor?

Ona göre vicdan doğuştan gelir, dayatılamaz oysa bugün pek çoğumuz
title: Rota: Bir Keçi Yolu mudur? | Zeliha Burtek | TEDxAtatürk University
